extra.message: In assert_attachment_access(), the branch handling dispute-linked attachments (if attachment.dispute_id:) immediately returns without performing any ownership or role check; the dead statement 'raise_if = False' and the comment indicate the authorization logic was disabled. Any authenticated user is therefore authorized for dispute evidence attachments whenever this fallback checker is consulted, allowing unauthorized download of other users' dispute files by ID (IDOR). Currently main.py's download_file routes dispute attachments through assert_dispute_access first, so this disabled check is a latent/fallback authorization gap, but the function itself grants blanket access.

extra.message: store_upload() reads the entire uploaded file into memory (content = upload.file.read()) before enforcing the 5MB size limit on the following line. An attacker can POST a very large body (e.g. multiple GB) to /api/products/{id}/image or /api/disputes/{id}/evidence and the server will buffer it fully in RAM before rejecting it, enabling memory-exhaustion denial of service. The size check must be enforced while streaming the upload.

extra.message: csv_response() writes field values into CSV cells without neutralizing formula characters (=, +, -, @, tab, CR). The /api/export/{kind} endpoint exports attacker-influenced strings (product names/descriptions and vendor names set by vendor managers, dispute reasons set by buyers, buyer emails) into these cells, so a value like '=HYPERLINK("http://evil","click")' or '=cmd|/C calc!A0' executes as a formula when an admin opens the exported CSV in Excel/LibreOffice, leading to data exfiltration or command execution on the admin's workstation.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: The password-reset endpoint records a fragment of the newly generated password reset token in the audit log (details={'mock_email_token': user.password_reset_token[:8]}). extra.message: The application secret key defaults to the well-known constant 'dev-secret-change-me'. A fail-fast requirement (no insecure default) should be enforced instead.
